correctness.rationale: The square-zero multiplication gives vertex diagonal bits and forbids loop coordinates in any idempotent. Diagonal interpolation forces distinct binary labels. Word-by-word telescoping proves the necessity of corner surjectivity, and commutators isolated by lifts of diagonal coordinate functions prove sufficiency. For a pair of labels at distance \(h\), the permitted \(h\) idempotent-coordinate columns restrict to a codimension-one kernel, so the exact number of full-rank corner maps is \(q^mR_q(h-1,m)\). Independence across arrow corners yields the displayed formula and probability. Positivity proves the binary-code threshold; the cube matching/even-parity argument proves the complete simple-clique cutoff. The finite checker enumerated 14 cases independently and passed. No finite enumeration is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Sampling uniformly from idempotents is mathematically motivated by their role as canonical generators and by Hu–Xiao’s qualitative theorem. The result computes an intrinsic finite-field generation statistic over an infinite family, shows that the optimal number of idempotents is field-size independent, and converts sharp generator thresholds for complete multi-arrow quivers to binary-code extremal capacities. Its two-vertex example demonstrates a genuine orientation-sensitive boundary invisible to total idempotent counts. These are structural, natural and potentially reusable invariants, rather than arbitrary small-count recomputations.
